summary: Build report pages bespoke and with soft-ui, then judge each pair blind for intent match

a_only: Run facts in a separate key-value panel (app, commit, start time, minutes, flows probed, probes, raw findings, verified); B puts the same facts in one subtitle line
A free-text search box in the top filter panel and a second search box above the table
A second set of filter dropdowns (severity, flow, dimension) on the table, which repeats the chip filter bar
Findings by flow as a vertical stacked bar chart
b_only: A written summary callout at the top: 2 critical, 5 high, checkout is the hot spot with both criticals, and 3 security issues span checkout, cart and account
Heatmap cells that filter the list when you click them
A 'Clear filters' link and a 'Showing N of 14' count beside the table
Table sorted with the worst first (critical, then high, medium, low); A's table shows low first and the criticals last, although its spec asked for '-severity'
Findings by flow as a horizontal stacked bar chart
judge.why: Both pages give the same facts in the same order: severity stat tiles, a flow-by-kind heatmap coloured by worst severity, a stacked bar chart by flow, chip filters, and a findings table that expands to show repro steps and evidence. B serves a tech lead who has 5 minutes better: its summary states the hot spot first, and its table puts the two criticals at the top, but A's table puts them at the bottom.

tool.friction:
The spec rendered with "check ok" on the first run, and no "fixed" or "error" lines. Five points were unclear or missing:
1. Catalog: the catalog does not say whether `sort: -severity` on a table uses severity rank (critical > high > medium > low) or alphabetical order. I assumed rank and could not confirm it without opening the page or reading the scripts.
2. Data paths: the catalog does not say how a relative data path resolves. The brief told me that paths resolve from the folder of the spec, and I needed that to write ../../../reports/R1-probe/findings.json.
3. kv list values: `kv` with a list value (flows_probed) has no documented display, such as comma-joined text or chips.
4. Run summary: I wanted a run-funnel line (31 raw findings, then 14 verified, from 25 probes) as one compact visual, but I found no funnel or ratio component. A meter (verified out of raw) could do part of it, but it would need inline values when a file holds the data.
5. Expanded rows: `expand` on a table shows repro and evidence, but I could not set a per-column fmt for the expanded fields. For example, I wanted evidence as code and repro as a numbered list with its newlines kept. I also could not tell whether a clicked heatmap cell (flow x dimension) filters on both axes or on one axis.

a_only: The 9 numbered use-case steps are visible below the sequence diagram, and the arrows carry matching step numbers (B keeps the steps in a folded 'Steps' tab)
Where each data contract is used or returned (for example 'returned by PreferenceEngine.decide')
A 'Changes' count for each component inside the components table
A discussion note that 'Move user prefs to a new service' lands in UserDirectory, which the design rates low volatility
States plainly that the design does not name the second component touched by the retry change
A legend for component kind and volatility, and a note that every call goes one way, down the layers
b_only: A warning banner at the top that puts the retry-with-backoff exception first
The retry banner names ChannelAccess as the second component, but design.json gives only a count of 2, so B made up that detail
A data-contract class diagram with reference edges (DeliveryResult to Message to Event) in place of four type cards
A 'Changes per component' bar chart beside the change table
The components table groups rows by kind and folds each group
The change table is sorted by components touched, so the exception is the first row
judge.why: Page A gives the reviewers the full use-case flow with numbered steps they can see, and contracts that show where each one is used. Page A also reports the retry exception honestly as an open question, but Page B names a second component that the data does not give. Page B puts the exception first, which helps, but it hides the steps in a tab and turns the contracts into a reference graph that says less about where each type is used.

error_lines: Error: YAML syntax error at line 2, column 38: mapping values are not allowed here. Hint: quote a value that has ": " in it, e.g. text: "a: b".
error layout[3].section[0].tabs[1].list: data file "d.core_use_case.steps" not found (looked in /home/user/pskills/soft-ui/eval/runs/full/R3-design)
tool.friction: 1) The `data: {d: design.json}` form registers only the top-level arrays (d.components, d.calls, d.contracts, d.change_simulation). It does not register arrays nested inside an object, such as core_use_case.steps. Writing `d.core_use_case.steps` failed with a misleading "data file not found" error, and the error gave no hint about the `file.json#a.b` form. Guessing `design.json#core_use_case.steps` worked. 2) A string array turns into rows with one column named `value`, and the catalog does not say so. The steps table has no step number column, and I found no "numbered list from data" option. 3) No component draws a sequence diagram from data. The steps are prose, so I wrote the Mermaid sequenceDiagram by hand, which copies the data into the spec. 4) No component draws a class or type diagram from data. Contracts hold `fields` arrays, and I was not sure how a table shows an array cell. So I wrote a Mermaid classDiagram by hand, which also copies the data. A `classes` or `types` component that takes {type, fields[]} rows would avoid this. 5) The tone map key for a numeric column (components_touched: {1: good, 2: warn}) went through without an error or fix line, but nothing confirms that integer keys match. 6) The stats tiles are hand-typed counts. stats `by` can count rows, but no tile shows the row count of a dataset, such as the number of components, and no tile counts rows matching a condition, such as "lands in one place, 6 / 7". 7) A small cost: the subtitle had a colon in it, and YAML failed until I quoted it. The hint was clear. 8) I did not view the page visually. I trusted "check ok", so the graph's box-by-kind layout with TD direction and the 3:2 width split are not checked by eye. The bespoke.html was not opened.

a_only: Separate 'Pull request' key-value panel (author, base, head, commits, verdict)
Full comment text for each finding in the findings table (B shows only title and file:line there)
Severity counts as separate HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW stat tiles
b_only: Total lines changed stat (+34 -4) and a Commits stat tile
Per-file finding chips (C1, C2...) in the files table and on each diff file header, linking findings to files
Gutter markers on the exact lines that carry a finding
Verdict as a badge in the header with the summary as a quote, not a coloured callout
judge.why: The two pages give the same verdict, severity counts, files table with change bars, findings ranked most serious first, and diff with each finding inline at its line, so the author takes away the same thing in the same order. B serves the author slightly better: it puts findings beside the files and tags each file with its finding IDs, while A repeats the PR metadata in a panel and the comment text in a wide table.

tool.friction:
All three renders printed "check ok", but the check missed two layout and sorting problems. I found both only by taking my own headless Chrome screenshot.

(1) The table sort direction for severity is reversed. "sort: -severity" put low first and high last, and "sort: severity" put high first. The severity rank is ascending from most serious, but neither the catalog nor explain says so. An agent that writes "-severity" for "most serious first" gets the wrong order with no warning.

(2) In a three-child row (kv, chart, table), the files table was clipped. It needed a horizontal scroll, so the added and removed columns were hidden. "check ok" and "fits a 400px phone" did not flag this overflow at desktop width. I removed the chart and gave the table w: 2. The chart only repeated the table's inline bars.

(3) The inline bars for "added" and "removed" are both blue. There is no green/red (good/bad) colouring for diff counts, and the table has no clear prop for a bar colour per column.

(4) The data paths resolve from the spec folder, so the spec points at ../../../reports/R5-pr/. That is correct but clumsy. At first I copied the data next to the spec, then removed the copies.

(5) To show the verdict as a callout, I had to type the summary text from pr.json into the spec by hand. callout cannot read a field from a dataset (for example pr.summary), and kv cannot give the verdict a tone.

(6) The SKILL says that render loads the page in a browser, but it gives the agent no screenshot or a way to look at the page. I had to find google-chrome myself to check the layout.

Everything in the brief is shown: the verdict, files changed and by how much, the full diff, and each finding inline at its line, plus a severity-sorted findings table. A small wish: each finding in the findings table could link to its note in the diff.
